newsitem.title: USA: ITT Hartford faces environmental charge - analyst.
newsitem.headline: ITT Hartford faces environmental charge - analyst.

text.p: Lehman analyst Peter Wade said he expects ITT Hartford Group Inc to announce third quarter charges to boost its reserves for asbestos and environmental losses and for losses on investment contracts.
Wade said he expects the company to announce a $440 million after-tax charge, or about $3.75 a share, when it announces third quarter earnings on October 18.
Wade said he raised his 1997 earnings estimate for ITT Hartford to $6.40 a share from $5.30, saying the charges would reduce the drag on earnings.
ITT Hartford shares rose 3/8 to 58-1/4.
ITT Hartford declined immediate comment on the matter.
In August, ITT Hartford said it had launched a study of its asbestos and environmental liabilities, which it expected to complete by the end of the year.
ITT Hartford at that time said it was too early to know whether it would boost its $1.3 billion in reserves for pollution claims as a result of the study.
The company earlier Thursday announced it expected losses from Hurricane Fran to total about $35 million after tax for the third quarter, or about $0.30 a share.
Wade said his 1997 estimate includes increased financing costs of just over $0.05 a share.
He said he expects the company to raise non-dilutive capital to offset the impacts of the reserve charges. He said he expects the company to issue about $500 million of equity-like capital.
Wade also said he repeated his buy recommendation on ITT Hartford and has a June 1997 price target of $70 a share.
Earnings of $6.40 a share in 1997 would allow ITT Hartford to generate 17 percent return on investment, he said.
Wade said he was confident that ITT Hartford will take both the environmental and investment contract charges in 1996, most likely in the third quarter.
He said his confidence stems from the company's decision to push up the date for the release of its earnings to October 18 from November 1.
In addition, he cited Standard & Poor's downgrade Wednesday of ITT Hartford units' claims-paying ability ratings and ITT Hartford's announcement Wednesday of a shelf offering of up to $1.25 billion.
S&P's downgrade "may indicate that the rating agency is aware of a reserve charge, meaning the charge can not be far off," Wade said in a report to the sales force.

In addition, Wade said, he believes the company's new management will want to start 1997 with a clean slate and the old management will want to leave the new management unencumbered by past liabilities.
ITT Hartford last week said it named Ramani Ayer to succeed Donald Frahm as chairman, president and chief executive, effective February 1, 1997.

ITT Hartford also said Lon Smith would become vice chairman of The Hartford unit on February 1. He would also maintain his current responsibilities as president and chief operating officer of worldwide life insurance operations.

Wade also said he believes ITT Hartford over the medium-term may examine splitting its property-casualty and life insurance operations, a move that could boost the value of ITT Hartford shares to $80 from fair value of about $65.

Smith, who runs the life insurance operations, would likely play a key role in determining the feasibility of such a move and would likely run the life insurance business if it should become a separate entity, Wade said.
